mainTopic: Conditions on a גט: תנאי כפול, changing conditions, and the משנה of 'if I do not return within thirty days'
overview: This amud first closes the earlier debate between רבא and רב אשי. רבא explains both clauses of the משנה, but רב אשי is left with a קשיא. A ברייתא then brings a dispute about conditions: רבי מאיר says a condition counts only if it is stated both ways (תנאי כפול), while the חכמים say a simple 'on condition that' is enough. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל notes that every condition in the Torah is doubled, and the גמרא gives two versions of whom he was arguing against. A second ברייתא seems to flip both sides. The גמרא resolves it: רבי מאיר's case had a doubled condition, and the 'חכמים' there are really רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who says a block not caused by the woman does not stop the גט. Another ברייתא teaches that a second, different condition gives her a choice, while a higher money demand cancels the first, and witnesses from different pairs cannot be joined. A new משנה then deals with 'if I do not come back within thirty days' and a husband who reaches a border town and returns. The גמרא begins asking whether אנטיפרס is in the גליל, citing a ברייתא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבא's view fits both clauses of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that according to רבא, the two clauses of the משנה describe two different cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well according to רבא: the first clause is where the husband did not state a time period, and the latter clause is where he did state one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. It first shows how easily רבא explains the משנה so that it can next ask why רב אשי cannot do the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the רישא and the סיפא are clearly different cases. In the רישא the husband just said 'serve my father' with no time. In the סיפא he said 'two years'. Because the cases differ, it makes sense that the משנה rules differently in each.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well (according to…). This sets up a contrast with a view that has a problem.
The first clause of the משנה
The latter clause of the משנה
He stated it explicitly (here: he stated the time period)

steps.confusionAlert: 'בשלמא' does not mean the גמרא is ruling like רבא. It only means 'this view has no problem here', to set up the problem for the other view.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rava,
the first clause is where he did not specify,
phrases.notes: He means the husband didn't say how long she must serve or nurse.

phrases.english: the latter clause is where he did specify.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the contrast between רבא and רב אשי by showing that רבא's reading works.
steps.kashyaTarget: Preparing a challenge against רב אשי's reading of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבא can tell the two clauses apart, רב אשי should be able to as well. The next step shows that he cannot.

steps.title: רב אשי cannot explain the difference between the clauses
steps.stepSummary: According to רב אשי, the גמרא cannot find what separates the רישא from the סיפא, and the question stays unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רב אשי, what is different about the first clause, and what is different about the latter clause? It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אשי. Under his view it cannot tell the two clauses apart, so it leaves the question as an unresolved difficulty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי holds that when no time is stated, even one day of serving or nursing is enough. That makes it hard to say what the רישא is talking about and why its ruling differs from the סיפא. The word 'קשיא' means the question stands with no answer, but רב אשי's view is not formally thrown out.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference? (asking why two cases are treated differently)
It is difficult. The question is left unanswered.

steps.whatToRemember: רבא explains the משנה smoothly. רב אשי is left with an unanswered 'קשיא' about the difference between the רישא and the סיפא.
steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' is weaker than 'תיובתא'. It means the problem is left open, not that רב אשי's view is fully refuted.

phrases.english: But according to Rav Ashi,
what is different about the first clause,
and what is different about the latter clause?
It is difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְרַב אָשֵׁי מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא וּמַאי שְׁנָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge set up in step 1 by turning to רב אשי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's view that, with no time stated, one day is enough
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רב אשי, the משנה's two clauses have no clear difference between them, yet the משנה rules differently in each.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The difficulty against רב אשי remains unresolved.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: a condition not stated both ways is void
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings רבי מאיר's view: if the husband did not state the condition both ways, the גט is valid even if the condition was not kept.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If he said, 'This is your גט on condition that you serve my father for two years,' or 'on condition that you nurse my son for two years,' then even if the condition was not fulfilled, it is a valid גט. This is because he did not say to her 'if you serve… and if you do not serve…' or 'if you nurse… and if you do not nurse…'. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא. רבי מאיר rules that a condition only counts if it is stated both ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר requires a תנאי כפול. The husband must spell out both what happens if she does it and what happens if she doesn't. Since this husband only said 'on condition that…', his condition has no force, and the גט works no matter what she does.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught. This introduces a ברייתא.
A 'doubled' condition, stated both ways: if yes and if not

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר is not saying that serving or nursing doesn't matter in general. He is saying that this particular wording, without the 'if not' half, fails to make a binding condition.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of תנאי כפול is a foundational idea for conditions throughout ש״ס, in גיטין, קידושין and more.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"This is your bill of divorce

phrases.aramaic: עַל מְנָת שֶׁתְּשַׁמְּשִׁי אֶת אַבָּא שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים״,
phrases.english: on condition that you serve my father for two years,"

phrases.aramaic: וְ״עַל מְנָת שֶׁתָּנִיקִי אֶת בְּנִי שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים״ –
phrases.english: or "on condition that you nurse my son for two years" —

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נִתְקַיֵּים הַתְּנַאי,
phrases.english: even though the condition was not fulfilled,
this is a valid bill of divorce;
because he did not say to her:
"If you serve — if you do not serve";
phrases.notes: He means stating both outcomes: if you serve, it's a גט; if you don't, it isn't.

phrases.english: "If you nurse — and if you do not nurse";
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן הֲרֵי זֶה גִּיטִּיךְ עַל מְנָת שֶׁתְּשַׁמְּשִׁי אֶת אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא on the same type of condition (serving the father, nursing the son).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, a condition not stated both ways is void, and the גט is valid even if the condition was not kept.

steps.title: The Sages: the condition counts even without double wording
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר: if the condition was kept the גט is valid, and if not, it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Sages say: if the condition was fulfilled, it is a valid גט; and if not, it is not a valid גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the opposing view of the חכמים, who do not require the condition to be stated both ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, simply saying 'on condition that…' is enough to make a real condition. So the גט depends entirely on whether she actually serves or nurses as required.

keyTerms.meaning: And the Sages say. This introduces the majority's opposing view.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
if the condition was fulfilled — it is a valid bill of divorce,
and if not — it is not a valid bill of divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים נִתְקַיֵּים הַתְּנַאי הֲרֵי זֶה גֵּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the view that disagrees with רבי מאיר in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The condition is binding even without double wording, so the גט depends on whether the condition was fulfilled.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: every Torah condition is doubled
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל notes that every condition found in the Torah is stated both ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: there is no condition in the Scriptures that is not doubled.
steps.whatsHappening: A third voice in the ברייתא points to the Torah's own pattern: its conditions are always stated both ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל draws attention to how conditions appear in the written Torah. Every one of them spells out both the 'if yes' and the 'if not'. The ברייתא does not say which side this supports. The next steps give two versions.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר says a condition needs double wording, and without it the גט is valid regardless. The חכמים say a simple 'on condition that' is enough. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל notes that every condition in the Torah is doubled.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
you do not have a condition in the Scriptures
that is not doubled.
phrases.notes: 'Doubled' means stated both ways: what happens if it's done, and what happens if it isn't.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר אֵין לְךָ תְּנַאי בַּכְּתוּבִים שֶׁאֵינוֹ כָּפוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third statement to the ברייתא about the Torah's pattern of conditions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every condition in the Torah is stated both ways.

steps.title: Two versions of whom רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was answering
steps.stepSummary: There are two versions: one says רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was speaking to רבי מאיר, the other says he was speaking to the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say he was speaking to רבי מאיר, and some say he was speaking to the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which side רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's remark from the last step was aimed at, and gives two possible answers. This sets up the next two steps, which explain each version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's remark that every Torah condition is doubled could be aimed at either side. If he is answering רבי מאיר, he is pushing back on him by saying we cannot learn from those verses. If he is answering the רבנן, he is pushing back on them by saying we do learn from those verses that a condition must be doubled.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say: a way of bringing a different version
The Rabbis, the same group as the חכמים
He is saying to him, meaning his words are aimed at that person

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר קָאָמַר לֵיהּ;
phrases.english: There are those who say: he is speaking to Rabbi Meir;
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, from his remark in the previous step.

phrases.english: and there are those who say: he is speaking to the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר קָאָמַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which side of the dispute in steps 3-4 the remark in step 5 belongs to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two versions of whom רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was addressing.

steps.title: Version one: he is answering רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: Since every condition in the Torah is doubled, those verses are 'two verses that come as one', and such verses do not teach a general rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to those who say he is speaking to רבי מאיר, he is telling him: every condition in the Torah is doubled, so they are like two verses that teach the same thing, and two such verses do not teach about other cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first version. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל tells רבי מאיר that he cannot learn a general rule from the Torah's doubled conditions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר learned from the Torah's examples that a condition must be stated both ways. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל answers that there is more than one such example, all saying the same thing. By the rule of 'two verses that come as one', that tells us they apply only to their own cases. So the requirement of a doubled condition falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubled condition: stated both ways, 'if you do it… and if you don't…'
Two verses that teach the same rule
They do not teach: we cannot extend them to other cases

steps.confusionAlert: In this version רבן שמעון בן גמליאל agrees that every Torah condition is doubled. He is arguing against learning from that fact, not against the fact itself.

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר קָאָמַר לֵיהּ –
phrases.english: Those who say he is speaking to Rabbi Meir —
this is what he is saying to him:
You have no condition in the verses
that is not doubled,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָווּ לְהוּ שְׁנֵי כְתוּבִים הַבָּאִין כְּאֶחָד,
phrases.english: so they become two verses that come as one,
phrases.notes: Meaning there is more than one place in the Torah teaching this same point.

phrases.english: and any two verses that come as one —
do not teach.
phrases.notes: They don't teach a rule for other cases, like a גט.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר קָאָמַר לֵיהּ – וְהָכִי קָאָמַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first version mentioned in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Torah's doubled conditions are 'two verses that come as one' and do not teach a general requirement of doubling.

steps.title: Version two: he is answering the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: Every condition in the Torah is doubled, and we do learn from them that a condition must be doubled.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to those who say he is speaking to the רבנן, he is telling them: every condition in the Torah is doubled, and we learn from those verses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second version. Here רבן שמעון בן גמליאל tells the רבנן that the Torah's doubled conditions are a source we can learn from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the same fact, that every Torah condition is doubled, works the other way. It becomes a reason to learn from those verses that a condition only works if it is doubled. This supports רבי מאיר's position against the רבנן.

phrases.english: Those who say he is speaking to the Rabbis —
this is what he is saying to them:
You have no condition in the verses
that is not doubled,
and we learn from them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי לְרַבָּנַן קָאָמַר לְהוּ – וְהָכִי קָאָמַר לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second version, the opposite reading of step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We learn from the Torah's doubled conditions that every condition must be doubled.
steps.whatToRemember: The same remark of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל can be read either way. Answering רבי מאיר, it means we cannot learn from the verses. Answering the רבנן, it means we can.

steps.title: A ברייתא where רבי מאיר says the גט is invalid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: a גט given on condition that she serve his father or nurse his son for two years, and the father or son died. רבי מאיר says it is not a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא contrasts this with a ברייתא: if the husband said 'This is your גט on condition that you serve my father two years' or 'nurse my son two years', and the father or the son died, it is not a גט. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a contradiction by bringing a ברייתא with the opposite-looking positions. Here רבי מאיר holds the גט is invalid because the condition was not kept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 3, רבי מאיר said that if a condition was not stated both ways, the גט stands even if the condition was not kept. Here the husband stated the condition only one way, yet רבי מאיר says the גט is invalid. That is the tension the גמרא is about to work on.

keyTerms.meaning: And they set them against each other: brings a contradicting source
That you serve, take care of

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
'This is your bill of divorce

phrases.aramaic: עַל מְנָת שֶׁתְּשַׁמְּשִׁי אֶת אַבָּא שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים״;
phrases.english: on condition that you serve my father for two years';

phrases.aramaic: ״עַל מְנָת שֶׁתָּנִיקִי אֶת בְּנִי שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים״ –
phrases.english: 'on condition that you nurse my son for two years' —
if the father died or the son died,
it is not a bill of divorce;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the explanation of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל to a source that seems to clash with the earlier ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's ruling in step 3 that a condition not stated both ways does not hold back the גט.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Here a condition stated only once does hold back the גט according to רבי מאיר, which seems to be the reverse of his earlier view.

steps.title: The חכמים in the ברייתא say the גט is valid
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say the גט is valid even though the condition was not kept, because she could say: 'Give me your father and I will serve him; give me your son and I will nurse him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: even though the condition was not kept, it is a גט, because she can tell him, 'Give me your father and I will serve him,' or 'Give me your son and I will nurse him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the חכמים, who rule that the גט is valid. This completes the contradiction, which the גמרא will spell out next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4 the חכמים said a גט is invalid if the condition was not kept. Here they say it is valid even though it was not kept. Their reason is that she was ready to do her part; the death was not her fault. So both sides seem to have switched positions from the earlier ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: She is able to say: she has a valid claim

steps.whyThisMatters: This contradiction forces the גמרא to explain how each side's view of conditions fits both ברייתות, and that drives the next part of the סוגיא.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נִתְקַיֵּים הַתְּנַאי,
phrases.english: even though the condition was not fulfilled,
it is a bill of divorce —
she can say to him:
'Give me your father, and I will serve him';
'Give me your son, and I will nurse him.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נִתְקַיֵּים הַתְּנַאי, הֲרֵי זֶה גֵּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 9 with the opposing view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים's ruling in step 4 that a גט is invalid if the condition was not kept.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Here the חכמים say the גט is valid even though the condition was not kept, which seems to be the reverse of their earlier view.

steps.title: Each side seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא about serving the father or nursing the son seems to contradict what רבי מאיר and the רבנן said earlier about doubled conditions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר seems to contradict himself, and the רבנן seem to contradict themselves!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets the new ברייתא next to the earlier statements about doubled conditions. It shows that both sides seem to say opposite things in the two places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי מאיר held that a condition only counts if it is doubled. So an ordinary condition should not hold up the גט, yet here he says 'it is not a גט.' The רבנן held earlier that a condition counts even without doubling, yet here they say the גט is valid even though the condition was not kept.

phrases.english: There is a difficulty: רבי מאיר against רבי מאיר,
phrases.notes: In the earlier source he needed a doubled condition. Here he lets an ordinary condition stop the גט.

phrases.english: and a difficulty: the Rabbis against the Rabbis!

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר אַדְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא brought in steps 9-10 to attack the earlier positions on doubled conditions
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of רבי מאיר and of the רבנן on whether a condition must be doubled
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each side's ruling in the new ברייתא seems to be the reverse of its earlier stance on doubled conditions.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: one case was doubled, the other was not
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction in רבי מאיר. In the earlier case the condition was not doubled, and in this case it was.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר does not contradict himself. There, he did not double his condition. Here, he did double it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the first half of the question by saying the two cases are not the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier case the condition was stated only once, so for רבי מאיר it does not count and the גט works. In our ברייתא we assume the husband did double it, so the condition counts. Since it was not kept, it is not a גט. The ברייתא simply did not mention the doubling.

keyTerms.meaning: He doubled his condition, stating both the 'if yes' and the 'if not'

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר אַדְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר לָא קַשְׁיָא –
phrases.english: רבי מאיר against רבי מאיר is not difficult:
there, it is where he did not double his condition;
here, it is where he did double his condition.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר אַדְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first half of the contradiction in step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (doubled versus not doubled)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources deal with the same kind of condition, so רבי מאיר contradicts himself
steps.terutzMaskana: Our ברייתא is speaking of a doubled condition, which רבי מאיר agrees is binding

steps.title: The חכמים here are really רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction in the רבנן, because the 'חכמים' of this ברייתא are רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. He holds that if the block to keeping the condition does not come from her, the גט is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis do not contradict themselves. Who are the חכמים here? It is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who said: any hindrance that is not from her, it is a valid גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second half by saying this unnamed view belongs to a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The regular רבנן would say an unkept condition stops the גט. But the 'חכמים' in this ברייתא are רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. He rules that if she was stopped by something that is not her fault, such as the father or son dying, the גט still works. So no single opinion is saying two opposite things.

keyTerms.meaning: Who are the Sages? A way of naming the real author of an unnamed view
A hindrance; something that prevents the condition from being kept
That is not from her; not caused by her
A תנא whose rule is that a block not caused by her does not stop the גט

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר is consistent because our case had a doubled condition. The רבנן are consistent because this ruling is really רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's rule: a block not caused by the woman does not stop the גט.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis against the Rabbis is not difficult,
for who are the חכמים here?

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הִיא, דְּאָמַר:
phrases.english: It is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who said:
Any hindrance that is not from her,
it is a valid גט.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן אַדְּרַבָּנַן לָא קַשְׁיָא, מַאן חֲכָמִים דְּהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second half of the contradiction in step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the author (the unnamed view belongs to a specific תנא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'חכמים' here are the same רבנן who hold an unkept condition stops the גט
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'חכמים' are רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who holds a block not from her does not stop the גט

steps.title: Two different conditions: she may fulfill either one
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: the husband gives one condition, then later a different condition in front of other witnesses. The second does not cancel the first, so she may fulfill whichever she wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If he said to her in front of two witnesses, 'Here is your גט on condition that you serve my father two years,' and then he said to her in front of two others, 'Here is your גט on condition that you give me two hundred זוז,' the later words do not cancel the first. If she wants, she serves him; if she wants, she gives him two hundred זוז.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic within conditional גיטין by quoting a ברייתא about a husband who states two different conditions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might think the second condition replaces the first. The ברייתא says no: both stay in force. She gets a choice, and keeping either one makes the גט valid.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; this opens a ברייתא
Two hundred זוז, a sum of money

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a new condition does not automatically wipe out an earlier one. The result is a choice between them.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן, אָמַר לָהּ בִּפְנֵי שְׁנַיִם:
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: If he said to her in front of two people:
'Here is your גט on condition
that you serve my father for two years,'
and then he went back and said to her in front of two people:
phrases.notes: This is a second pair of witnesses, not the same two as before.

phrases.aramaic: ״הֲרֵי זֶה גִּיטִּךְ עַל מְנָת שֶׁתִּתְּנִי לִי מָאתַיִם זוּז״ –
phrases.english: 'Here is your גט on condition that you give me two hundred זוז' —

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בִּיטֵּל דִּבְרֵי הָאַחֲרוֹן אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹן;
phrases.english: the later words did not cancel the first;
if she wants, she serves him,
if she wants, she gives him two hundred זוז.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן, אָמַר לָהּ בִּפְנֵי שְׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion of conditional גיטין after the contradictions were resolved
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A second, different condition does not cancel the first. She may fulfill either one.

steps.title: A second, bigger money demand cancels the first
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. If the husband first demands 200 זוז in front of two witnesses, and later demands 300 זוז in front of two others, the later demand cancels the first. Also, one witness from each pair cannot be joined together to make a set of two.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he told her in front of two people, 'This is your גט on condition that you give me 200 זוז,' and then told her in front of two others, 'This is your גט on condition that you give me 300 זוז,' the later words cancel the earlier ones. One witness from the first pair and one from the second pair do not join together.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from step 14 keeps going and gives a contrasting case. This time the second condition is about the same thing as the first, just a bigger amount of money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14 the two conditions were about different things, so both stayed in force and she could choose. Here the second condition only raises the price, so the first one is gone. The ברייתא ends with a rule that one witness from each pair cannot be counted together.

keyTerms.meaning: in front of two people (two witnesses)
they join together (to count as one set of witnesses)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 14. There the two conditions were different, so both stayed. Here the second one only changes the amount, so it replaces the first.

phrases.english: But if he said to her in front of two people:
"This is your bill of divorce

phrases.aramaic: עַל מְנָת שֶׁתִּתְּנִי לִי מָאתַיִם זוּז״,
phrases.english: on condition that you give me two hundred zuz,"
and then he went back and said to her in front of two others:
"This is your bill of divorce

phrases.aramaic: עַל מְנָת שֶׁתִּתְּנִי לִי שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת זוּז״ –
phrases.english: on condition that you give me three hundred zuz"
the later words cancel the first;
and one of the first pair
and one of the later pair do not join together.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל אָמַר לָהּ בִּפְנֵי שְׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 14 with a contrasting case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the second condition only raises the money, it cancels the first. Witnesses from the two different pairs cannot be joined together.

steps.title: Which case is the 'do not join' line about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which part of the ברייתא the witness rule refers to. It cannot be the last case, because there the first condition is already cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which case is this about? If you say it is about the last case, the first condition was already cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which case the line 'witnesses do not join together' belongs to. It immediately rules out the last case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last case the first condition no longer exists. So there is nothing for the first pair of witnesses to join with. Saying the rule there would teach us nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: on which one? (which case is this about?)
the last part of a teaching

phrases.english: On which case is this said?
phrases.notes: This is asking about the line that says one witness from each pair can't be joined together.

phrases.english: If you say on the last case, it is already cancelled!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַהֵיָיא? אִילֵּימָא אַסֵּיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks where the closing line of the ברייתא from step 15 belongs.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case of the ברייתא the rule about not joining witnesses refers to.

steps.title: It belongs to the first case
steps.stepSummary: Since the last case does not work, the rule must be about the first case, where two different conditions both stay in force.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is about the first case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The witness rule refers to the first case from step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case both conditions are still valid. So one could have thought that the witnesses could be joined. That is why the rule is needed there.

keyTerms.meaning: the first part of a teaching

phrases.english: Rather, on the first case.
phrases.notes: This is the case from step 14, where the second condition was about something different.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אַרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule about not joining witnesses refers to the first case, where both conditions remain.

steps.title: But that is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the rule is obvious even in the first case. Each pair saw a different condition, so of course they cannot be joined.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 17. Why would the ברייתא need to tell us something so obvious?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each pair of witnesses heard a different condition. One witness from each pair never saw the same thing. So why teach that they cannot be counted together?

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the rule once it is placed on the first case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that witnesses from the two pairs do not join, read as referring to the first case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The witnesses saw different conditions, so not joining them is obvious and did not need to be taught.

steps.title: One might have thought all condition witnesses join
steps.stepSummary: The rule is needed because one might have thought that all witnesses who testify that there was a condition can be joined together. The ברייתא teaches that they cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that all those who testify to set up a condition join together. So it teaches us that they do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of step 18. It shows the mistake the ברייתא is protecting us from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think that the witnesses only need to show that the גט came with some condition. Then any two of the four could be counted. The ברייתא teaches that each condition needs its own full pair of witnesses.
steps.whatToRemember: A later condition that only raises the price cancels the earlier one. When two different conditions both stand, each one needs its own pair of witnesses. One witness from each pair cannot be combined.

phrases.english: You might have said,
all who testify to set up a condition join together;
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows a possible wrong assumption that the ברייתא rules out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the witnesses only need to show the גט was conditional, one witness from each pair could be counted together.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each condition needs its own full pair of witnesses. Witnesses of different conditions do not join.

steps.title: New משנה: 'If I don't come back in thirty days,' and he returns early
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. A husband says the גט takes effect if he does not come back within thirty days. He was traveling from יהודה to גליל, reached אנטיפרס, and came back. His condition is void.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'This is your גט if I do not come back from now until thirty days.' He was going from יהודה to גליל, reached אנטיפרס, and came back. His condition is cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives a case where the גט depends on the husband staying away for thirty days, but he comes back before then.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גט only takes effect if he does not return within thirty days. He returned within the time, so the condition for the divorce never happened. The משנה says his condition is void, so she is not divorced.

keyTerms.meaning: if I do not come back
אנטיפרס, a town on the way between יהודה and גליל

phrases.english: MISHNA:
"This is your bill of divorce

phrases.aramaic: אִם לֹא בָּאתִי מִכָּאן עַד שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם״,
phrases.english: if I do not come back from now until thirty days,"
and he was traveling from Judea to the Galilee;
he reached Antipatris and came back,
phrases.notes: The משנה seems to treat reaching אנטיפרס as reaching the גליל. The גמרא questions this in step 24.

phrases.english: his condition is cancelled.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הֲרֵי זֶה גִּיטִּךְ אִם לֹא בָּאתִי מִכָּאן עַד שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new type of condition, about time and travel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the husband conditions the גט on not returning within thirty days and returns early, the condition is void and she is not divorced.

steps.title: Traveling from the גליל to יהודה and turning back at כפר עותנאי
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives the mirror case of step 20. A husband traveling from גליל to יהודה makes the same thirty-day condition, reaches כפר עותנאי, and turns back. His condition is void.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said, 'This is your גט if I do not come back within thirty days,' and he was going from the גליל to יהודה, reached כפר עותנאי, and came back, his condition is void.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a second travel case. This time the husband goes the opposite direction, from גליל toward יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband reached the border of his destination region at כפר עותנאי and came back within the thirty days. So the condition 'if I do not come back' was not met. His condition is void, and a later, longer trip will not make the גט take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: The northern region of ארץ ישראל
The southern region of ארץ ישראל
A town at the edge of the גליל, on the way to יהודה

phrases.english: "This is your bill of divorce
if I do not come back from now
until thirty days,"
and he was going from the Galil to Yehuda,
and he reached Kefar Otnai and returned,
his condition is void.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי זֶה גִּיטִּיךְ אִם לֹא בָּאתִי מִכָּאן עַד שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם וְהָיָה הוֹלֵךְ מִגָּלִיל לִיהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror case of step 20, traveling in the opposite direction
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Turning back at כפר עותנאי on the way from גליל to יהודה cancels the thirty-day condition.

steps.title: Traveling overseas and turning back at עכו
steps.stepSummary: The same thirty-day condition is made by someone heading overseas. He reaches עכו and comes back, so his condition is void.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said, 'This is your גט if I do not come back within thirty days,' and he was going overseas, reached עכו, and came back, his condition is void.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a third travel case. Here the husband is heading overseas and turns back at the port city עכו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is the same as in the earlier cases. He reached עכו on his overseas trip and came back within the thirty days. So the condition was not met, and it stays void even if he later travels away for longer.

keyTerms.meaning: Akko, a port city where people boarded ships

phrases.english: "This is your bill of divorce
if I do not come back from now
until thirty days,"
and he was going to a country overseas,
and he reached Akko and returned,
his condition is void.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָיָה הוֹלֵךְ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם וְהִגִּיעַ לְעַכּוֹ וְחָזַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same rule to a trip overseas
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Turning back at עכו before sailing overseas cancels the thirty-day condition.
steps.whatToRemember: In all three travel cases, the condition belongs to one specific trip. If he reaches the border point of that trip and comes back within the thirty days, the condition is void, even if he later travels again.

steps.title: Any thirty days away: visits without being alone do not break it
steps.stepSummary: A husband says the גט takes effect any time he is away from her for thirty days. He kept going and coming. Since he was never alone with her, it is a valid גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said, 'This is your גט any time I am away from you for thirty days,' and he kept going and coming, it is a valid גט, because he was never alone with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a different kind of condition, which is not tied to one trip. It rules that his short visits do not stop the גט from taking effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This condition is about any thirty days away from her, so a cancelled trip changes nothing. His coming and going does not reset the count, because he was never alone with her. Since they had no real time together, the thirty days of separation are complete and the גט works.

phrases.english: "This is your bill of divorce
any time that I depart
from your presence for thirty days";
he was going and coming, going and coming,
since he was not alone with her,
this is a valid bill of divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי זֶה גִּיטִּיךְ כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁאֶעֱבוֹר מִכְּנֶגֶד פָּנַיִךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts a general 'any thirty days' condition with the single-trip conditions
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under an 'any thirty days' condition, coming and going without being alone with her does not interrupt the thirty days, and the גט is valid.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this case up with the earlier ones. There, coming back cancels the condition. Here, coming back does not matter, because he was never alone with her.
steps.whatToRemember: The wording of the condition decides the outcome. A condition of 'if I do not come back within thirty days' is void once he comes back in time. A condition about any thirty days away is fulfilled when they were never alone together.

steps.title: Was אנטיפרס in the גליל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking whether the משנה means that אנטיפרס is in the גליל.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Does this mean that אנטיפרס was in the גליל?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by questioning the geography in the משנה's case of אנטיפרס from step 20. This sets up a contradiction that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 20, a man going from יהודה to גליל turned back at אנטיפרס. The משנה seems to treat reaching אנטיפרס as reaching the גליל. The exclamation shows the גמרא finds this hard to accept.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that comes after the משנה
Antipatris, a town on the road between יהודה and גליל

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Is this to say that Antipatris
was located in the Galil?!
phrases.notes: This goes back to step 20, where the man going from יהודה to גליל turned back at אנטיפרס.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּאַנְטִיפְרַס בְּגָלִיל הֲוָה קָיְימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins analyzing the משנה, starting with the אנטיפרס case
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's implied placement of אנטיפרס in the גליל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reading the משנה this way puts אנטיפרס in the גליל, and the גמרא is about to show a source that says otherwise.

steps.title: A ברייתא says אנטיפרס is in יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that contradicts the משנה. אנטיפרס is in יהודה, כפר עותנאי is in the גליל, and the area between them is treated strictly. The ruling begins 'she is divorced' and continues on the next amud, leaving her status in doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: They pointed out a contradiction: אנטיפרס is in יהודה, and כפר עותנאי is in the גליל. The area between them is treated strictly, and she is divorced...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that clashes with the משנה. The ברייתא places אנטיפרס in יהודה, not in the גליל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If אנטיפרס is in יהודה, reaching it does not mean he reached the גליל, so the משנה's reading is a problem. The ברייתא adds that the land between the two towns is treated strictly, as if it belongs to both regions. Because of that, her status is uncertain; the word 'מגורשת' only begins a sentence that continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: And they pointed out a contradiction between two sources

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
Antipatris is in Yehuda;
and Kefar Otnai is in the Galil;
the area between them is treated stringently,
she is divorced
phrases.notes: The ברייתא's sentence keeps going on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהִי אַנְטִיפְרַס בִּיהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that turns the question of step 24 into a real contradiction
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's case in step 20, which treats reaching אנטיפרס as reaching the גליל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says אנטיפרס is in יהודה, so a man who reached it never got to the גליל. That clashes with how the משנה uses אנטיפרס.
steps.whyThisMatters: Whether the condition was really tied to reaching a new region depends on where the border is, so this geography question affects whether the woman is divorced.
